Latin word

agnōscō

agnōscō, agnōscere, agnōvī, agnitum

verb, third conjugation

recognize, know again; acknowledge, own (as one’s own or as true)

In this lexicon

  • recognize

    the recommended word · classical · Quint. 11.2.17: nōn ipsa agnōscimus tantum; Cic. Fin. 5.42: eōs agnōscunt, ā quibus ēducantur

  • recognize

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 4.4.1: mē nōn esse verbōrum admodum inopem agnōscō; Cic. Fam. 5.20.5: id ego agnōvī meō jussū esse factum

Examples

  • nam cum in loca aliqua post tempus reversī sumus, nōn ipsa agnōscimus tantum, sed etiam, quae in hīs fēcerīmus, reminīscimur

    for when we go back to a place after some time, we not only recognise it but also remember what we did thereQuint. 11.2.17

    In the entry for recognize

  • excipiunt plausū pavidōs gaudentque tuentēs Dardanidae, veterumque agnōscunt ōra parentum

    the Trojans greet the nervous boys with applause and delight in watching them, and recognise in them the faces of their forebearsVerg. A. 5.575–576

    In the entry for recognize

  • et ego ipse … mē nōn esse verbōrum admodum inopem agnōscō

    and I myself admit that I am not altogether short of wordsCic. Fam. 4.4.1
